entities.summary: William Ronald Durnan was a Canadian professional ice hockey goaltender who played with the Montreal Canadiens in the National Hockey League (NHL) between 1943 and 1950. He was one of the best goaltenders in his time, winning the Vezina Trophy for fewest goals allowed six times, being named First All-Star team as best goaltender six times, and helping the Canadiens win the Stanley Cup twice. Durnan retired in 1950, citing the stress of playing professional hockey. However, in his final season he suffered a severe laceration of the scalp, but was only sidelined 12 days and returned heroically for the playoffs.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As one of the best goaltenders in his time, Bill Durnan's six Vezina Trophy wins and six First All-Star team selections had a significant impact on the Montreal Canadiens' success during the 1940s and 1950s. His heroic return from injury for the playoffs showcased his dedication to the sport.
